title: Hang an off-balance picture frame level on a pin by its sawtooth hanger
instruction: Hang the picture frame on the pin in the white board by the sawtooth hanger on its back, so that it hangs level by itself.
context: Hanging pictures, mirrors, signs and certificates level is everyday work for installers, art handlers, hotel fit-out crews and handymen. A frame on a single nail settles under its own weight, and a heavy object mounted off-centre (here a medal in the lower left of a shadow box) makes it hang crooked from the middle of its hanger: the worker has to watch how it hangs, lift it and move it along the hanger's teeth. Unlike leaning a frame on a ledge, the frame here hangs from one point and swings to its own balance.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Picture frame (dark-stained wood shadow box with glass, 0.5 kg in all): outer 30 cm wide, 15 cm tall, 3.5 cm deep. The glass, mat and backing fill its front 2 cm; behind them the moulding's 2 cm wide rails leave a 1.5 cm deep recess. A bronze medal (4 cm across, on a red ribbon) is fixed behind the glass in the lower left: 200 g, its centre 4.0 cm left of and 4.5 cm below the frame's centre, so the frame (300 g without it) has its centre of mass 1.6 cm left of and 1.8 cm below its centre. Sawtooth hanger (steel, screwed to the backing in the recess, centred under the top rail): a bar 9.6 cm long and 1 cm thick (front to back) with 12 teeth along its lower edge, 90-degree V-notches 8 mm apart and 4 mm deep, 11 notches in all; the middle notch is on the frame's centre line and the notches' tops are 2.8 cm below the frame's top. The frame starts standing upright, glass toward the robot, centred at (0.22, 0.00), in a grey stand: a 34 x 7.1 x 1.2 cm base plate (long side along y) with two 1.5 x 1.5 cm rails along its long edges, leaving a 4.1 cm slot (3 mm play each side). Board (white painted MDF, smooth): 2 cm thick, 10 cm wide, 22 cm tall, standing on the table across the x direction, its front face at x = 0.335, centred at y = 0.01. Pin: a 4 mm round steel pin, horizontal, sticking 13 mm out of the board's front face at y = 0.01, its axis 15.0 cm above the table. Hung from the notch 1.6 cm left of the hanger's middle, the frame hangs level with its rails against the board and its bottom 3.1 cm above the table. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: 0 if at any time the frame is dropped (its centre falls faster than 0.6 m/s, about a 2 cm free fall) or falls below the table top. Hanging means: the pin sits in one of the hanger's notches and carries the frame (nothing else holds it: every part of both arms at least 2 cm from the frame, and the frame's lowest corner at least 5 mm above the table). 1.0 (success): hanging, the frame's top edge within 2 degrees of horizontal (the two top corners within 1.05 cm of the same height), and still (under 1 cm/s and 3 degrees/s) for 1 s. Otherwise, at the end: 0.5 if hanging with the top edge within 10 degrees of horizontal; else 0.25 if at some point the frame was lifted to the board (its lowest corner at least 2 cm above the table while its rearmost point was within 3 cm of the board's face); else 0. Hung from the hanger's middle notch the frame tilts about 13 degrees, onto its low corner on the table (0.25); one notch off the level one, 7 degrees (0.5).
reset_notes: Lift the frame off the pin and stand it back in the stand's slot, glass toward the robot, centred. Check the pin is still horizontal and 15 cm up; a bent pin changes how the frame hangs.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The frame is one rigid body with its mass and centre of mass set to include the medal. The pin is a fixed 4 mm capsule; the board's painted face has low friction (0.1), so the frame can rest at most about 2 degrees off its balance (a gloss-painted board does the same). The hanger is 1 cm thick, thicker than a stamped one, so the 4 mm pin can catch it; a real one can be cut from aluminium bar.
